note.question: How do social learning and content quality interact under polarization?
note.overview: This paper studies how polarization influences content consumption and production on digital platforms that monetize consumer engagement. Specifically, we consider a content that advocates a particular position on a divisive issue. Consumers with polarized preferences toward the content’s position are sequentially exposed to the content.

components.formal: Feasibility rule: retain only decisions satisfying the stated resource and system restrictions.
conditions: First, when in-group consumers are the majority among the population (i.e., u > 1/2), the content gains popularity merely due to its position, regardless of its quality.
The opposite is true when in-group consumers are the minority (i.e., u < 1/2).
As the polarization level increases, this popularity effect gets stronger, thereby discouraging the content provider from improving the quality of the content.
